server start
# A status acknowledgment is a fence. The CLI replays the identical write and
# requires its actual response, without beginning another upload.
fault write-lost
skygo artifacts upload source
cp stdout first.json
calls ok:BeginArtifactUpload 1
calls ok:WriteArtifactChunk 2
calls GetArtifactUpload 1
# A completed Finalize response is lost; automatic recovery replays the same ID.
fault finalize-lost
skygo artifacts upload source
cp stdout second.json
upload-id UPLOAD
cp source/seed.txt original.txt
cp changed.txt source/seed.txt
! skygo artifacts upload source --resume $UPLOAD
stderr 'does not match the snapshot'
calls ok:WriteArtifactChunk 3
cp original.txt source/seed.txt
skygo artifacts upload source --resume $UPLOAD
cp stdout resumed.json
cmp second.json resumed.json
skygo artifacts download --ref resumed.json restored
cmp original.txt restored/seed.txt
calls ok:BeginArtifactUpload 2
calls GetArtifactUpload 3
calls ok:WriteArtifactChunk 3
# Finalize can also return Busy for its first publishing transition; its exact
# count depends on real physical sampling, so only the stable ID/ref is asserted.
calls SubmitWorkspaceJob 0
server stop
! stderr .
-- source/seed.txt --
seed
-- changed.txt --
changed
